final_answer: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing works by first designing a guide RNA that matches the target DNA sequence. This guide RNA directs the Cas9 enzyme to the specific location in the genome. Once there, Cas9 makes a double-strand break in the DNA. The cell then repairs this break through either non-homologous end joining or homology-directed repair, allowing for precise gene modifications.
